comparison: Both address circadian neutrophil infiltration and clock gene correlation (C1, C15, C16, C19, C27-C30). OpenEval finds claims well-supported by flow cytometry and qRT-PCR data. Peer reviewers acknowledge correlation but question causal 'control' relationship, noting Bmal1 still increases in neutropenic mice, suggesting uncertainty about mechanism strength.

OpenEval R2 addresses correlation between neutrophil infiltration and clock genes (C27-C30, C35) as supported. Peer R1 covers overlapping claims but expresses uncertainty about causality, questioning how neutropenic mice rescue jet lag phenotype if neutrophils control clock genes.

Both address in vitro neutrophil-hepatocyte interactions and elastase specificity (C36-C41). OpenEval finds claims supported by qRT-PCR and controls. Peer reviewers accept the neutrophil elastase mechanism without challenge, as reflected in acceptance summary.

Both address JNK pathway involvement (C75-C77, C79-C81, C83). OpenEval finds claims supported by immunoblot and genetic models. Peer reviewers accept the NE/JNK/Bmal1 mechanistic axis as stated in acceptance summary, indicating agreement.
OpenEval R9 addresses JNK knockout effects (C85-C87). Peer R3 broadly accepts JNK pathway mechanism. Both support the role of JNK in mediating neutrophil effects on hepatocyte metabolism.

Both address FGF21 involvement (C90-C96). OpenEval finds FGF21 knockdown provides critical functional evidence. Peer reviewers accept FGF21 as part of regulatory mechanism per acceptance summary, with no challenges to this pathway component.

Both address neutrophil infusion rescue experiments (C110-C113, C115). OpenEval finds strong causal evidence for NE-mediated effects. Peer reviewers specifically requested this experiment and data appears to satisfy their concern about demonstrating NE-dependent effects.

Both address NE knockout validation (C97-C103, C108-C109). OpenEval finds genetic validation strengthens elastase role. Peer reviewers accept NE knockout data without challenge, supporting elastase specificity.

Both address human liver sample correlations (C11, C13, C116-C118). OpenEval notes correlations are significant but modest cohort size (n=23) limits causal inference. Peer reviewers accept translational relevance without challenge in essential revisions.

Both address CXCL1 chemokine involvement (C23-C26). OpenEval notes speculation about functional role without direct testing. Peer reviewers accept anatomical and recruitment mechanism details without challenge.

Both address organ specificity of neutrophil effects (C45-C48). OpenEval finds organ-specific data strengthens liver-specific conclusion. Peer reviewers accept organ specificity without challenge, supporting local versus systemic effects.

Both address protective effects of reduced neutrophil infiltration across models (C4-C10, C42-C44, C121-C124). OpenEval finds consistency across models provides strong evidence. Peer reviewers express uncertainty due to Lyzs-Cre model affecting multiple myeloid cell types, questioning neutrophil specificity.

Both address jet lag experiments (C50-C57). OpenEval finds protective effect in neutropenic mice provides strong evidence. Peer reviewers question convincingness, noting Bmal1 still increases in neutropenic mice and requesting clarification on diet model rationale.

Both address diet-induced metabolic disruption (C58-C63). OpenEval finds differential response strengthens causal link. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about neutrophil control mechanism and question experimental design choices between HFD and MCD diets.

OpenEval R12 addresses NE knockout protection in diet models (C104-C109). Peer R5 addresses broader protective phenotype concerns. Both relate to metabolic protection, but peer reviewers question cell-type specificity of genetic models.
OpenEval R6 addresses CXCR2 and p38γ/δ knockout validation (C56-C57). Peer R6 broadly questions jet lag and diet experiments. Limited direct overlap, but both relate to genetic validation approaches.

OpenEval R15 addresses central mechanistic conclusions (C2-C3, C14, C73, C84, C118, C120, C126). Peer R3 accepts NE/JNK/Bmal1 mechanistic axis. Both support overall pathway with strong evidence from multiple approaches.
OpenEval R21 addresses JNK literature context (C74, C88-C89, C127-C136). Peer R3 accepts JNK pathway mechanism. Both support JNK's established role in liver metabolism.
OpenEval R21 includes FGF21 literature context (C88-C89, C136). Peer R4 accepts FGF21 mechanism. Both support FGF21's role in metabolic regulation.
OpenEval R24 addresses overarching conclusions including FGF21 (C123, C137-C140). Peer R4 accepts FGF21 mechanism. Both support final conclusions about NE-FGF21 axis.
OpenEval R1 includes neutrophil localization (C21-C22). Peer R9 accepts anatomical details. Minor overlap on spatial relationship between neutrophils and hepatocytes.

OpenEval R20 addresses p38γ/δ knockout model (C68-C72). Peer R6 questions jet lag experiments broadly. Both relate to genetic validation but peer reviewers express broader uncertainty about causal mechanisms.
OpenEval R25 marks elastase-JNK mechanism (C82) as uncertain due to lack of direct demonstration. Peer R3 accepts overall JNK pathway. OpenEval more cautious about specific mechanistic step.
OpenEval R26 notes uncertainty about specific correlation data (C12) in human samples. Peer R8 accepts human correlations without challenge. OpenEval identifies missing statistical details.

OpenEval R18 addresses literature-based metabolic context claims (C17-C18, C32-C34, C131). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these background claims not specifically discussed by reviewers.
OpenEval R19 addresses antibody depletion validation (C64-C67). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this alternative neutropenia approach not specifically discussed by reviewers.
OpenEval R22 addresses background literature context (C31, C39, C78, C124-C125). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these contextual claims not specifically discussed by reviewers.
OpenEval R23 addresses jet lag literature context (C49). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this background citation not specifically discussed by reviewers.
OpenEval R25 marks blood-liver neutrophil migration (C20) as uncertain without direct migration studies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific mechanistic detail.
